identity_binding_mechanism.evidence: The process may cause an issuance of an on-chain verification proof to the particular blockchain address.

identity_binding_mechanism.definition: Identity is bound by behavioural data from a device that satisfies a human-characteristic threshold, distinguishing humans from automated or duplicate devices.
identity_binding_mechanism.evidence: In response to determining that the behavioral data satisfies a human characteristic threshold

identity_binding_mechanism.definition: Identity or eligibility bound to a biological attribute such as DNA fingerprint or genetic relationship of a person.
identity_binding_mechanism.evidence: based on a combination of a DNA biological fingerprint of the person who originated the physical product instance

smart_contract_definition_scope.definition: Smart contract execution mode where results are computed but not written to the ledger when an expiration or simulation indicator is set.
smart_contract_definition_scope.evidence: check whether a simulation indicator has been set, which indicates that an expiration time of the first smart contract has been reached

smart_contract_definition_scope.definition: Hardware pipeline accelerating transaction signature and state validation for decentralized applications on a ledger.
smart_contract_definition_scope.evidence: fixed pipeline hardware architecture for processing transaction verification operations in decentralized applications

validator_selection_mechanism.definition: Validators chosen by computed node capability thresholds, with other nodes selected randomly to resist attacks and mining conflict.
validator_selection_mechanism.evidence: according to the threshold values, determining a current accounting node, and thereafter randomly selecting other nodes

validator_selection_mechanism.definition: Endorsement of transactions or participants determined by aggregating role-derived scores against a threshold rather than by a fixed set or consensus vote.
validator_selection_mechanism.evidence: aggregate the respective scores into an endorsement score

ecosystem_participant_role.definition: Blockchain patent scheme that selects the lowest-expense miner device to solve each block, optimising operating resources of miners.
ecosystem_participant_role.evidence: selecting an optimal cost miner device among the miner devices based on the identified expenses

privacy_enhancement.definition: Privacy scheme that replaces an already-written ledger transaction with concealed data such as its hash, rather than obfuscating it at creation.
privacy_enhancement.evidence: generating a concealment instruction comprising the target transaction identifier

privacy_enhancement.definition: Participant identity is replaced by an internal identifier mapped to the real identity to anonymise partners on the ledger.
privacy_enhancement.evidence: generating, by a processor node, an identifier (ID) for an asset producer node

ledger_storage_model.proposal: block pruning / truncation of historical blocks
ledger_storage_model.definition: Ledger storage model in which old blocks are truncated and replaced by a summary block capturing essential data, reducing storage.
ledger_storage_model.evidence: truncating one or more blocks with a time stamp that is older than a pre-determined cut-off time

ledger_storage_model.definition: Periodically generated snapshot of ledger state stored and agreed by peer nodes to increase blockchain efficiency.
ledger_storage_model.evidence: periodically generating a state database checkpoint

ledger_storage_model.definition: Ledger retains only recent blocks by deleting oldest blocks under a retention period and minimum block count, with a hash anchoring the remaining chain.
ledger_storage_model.evidence: a retention period (T), a minimum number of blocks (L), and a hash of the oldest block are defined

ledger_storage_model.definition: Ledger storage that splits blocks across nodes with a parity block so the full chain can be reconstructed if nodes fail.
ledger_storage_model.evidence: The system forms a parity block from the individual blocks striped from the single blockchain

ledger_storage_model.definition: Ledger stores only cryptographic proofs or hashes of data while the underlying data is maintained and removable within the system.
ledger_storage_model.evidence: The blockchain system stores cryptographic proofs of data on an immutable ledger.

ledger_storage_model.proposal: pruned blockchain with new genesis block
ledger_storage_model.definition: Ledger storage is reduced by pruning historical blocks and re-anchoring the chain at a new genesis block committing to Merkle roots of active state.
ledger_storage_model.evidence: A local copy of the blockchain is pruned at a pruning point in accordance with the pruning threshold parameter

ledger_storage_model.definition: Ledger storage model where historical blocks are pruned behind a new current genesis block, retaining only recent state for scalability.
ledger_storage_model.evidence: method for confirming configuration of a new current genesis block in a blockchain configured to enable pruning

ledger_storage_model.proposal: hybrid on-chain and off-chain file storage
ledger_storage_model.definition: Ledger stores only critical data or metadata on-chain while bulk data references are held in a distributed file system at addresses recorded in the block.
ledger_storage_model.evidence: Noncritical data elements in the data object are stored in data block files at an address on a distributed file system

risk_type_illicit_finance.proposal: security risk scoring of transfers via ML
risk_type_illicit_finance.definition: Risk assessed by machine-learning models over extracted smart contract features to permit or block cross-chain transfers.
risk_type_illicit_finance.evidence: generate machine learning models based on the extracted features to output a security risk threshold

risk_type_illicit_finance.definition: Risk assessed by scoring a transfer's destination address using ML-based pattern data before the user proceeds with the transaction.
risk_type_illicit_finance.evidence: generate a confidence score informed based on transaction pattern data for the destination address

risk_type_illicit_finance.definition: Unauthorised withdrawal of virtual assets from exchange-managed addresses, prevented by double payment prevention policies on withdrawal transactions.
risk_type_illicit_finance.evidence: blocking illegal withdrawal of a virtual asset by monitoring unapproved fraudulent transactions

risk_type_illicit_finance.proposal: abnormal/fraudulent transaction detection via deep learning on wallet transaction features
risk_type_illicit_finance.definition: Risk detection that classifies wallet transaction behaviour as abnormal or fraudulent using learned feature vectors compared against a reference value.
risk_type_illicit_finance.evidence: comparing the intermediate value to a predetermined reference value to determine if a fraudulent transaction

wallet_interface_delivery_form.definition: Physical object carrying authentication data that links to and grants access to an NFT's ownership record and associated digital asset.
wallet_interface_delivery_form.evidence: physical item may include authenticating information that enables the system to verify ownership of an NFT

wallet_interface_delivery_form.definition: Wallet keys held in an integrated circuit of a payment card, used to sign blockchain transactions presented at a point-of-sale terminal.
wallet_interface_delivery_form.evidence: storing, in an integrated circuit of a payment card, a first private key of a first cryptographic key pair

wallet_interface_delivery_form.definition: Wallet seed derived from a physically unclonable function response on a hardware device rather than stored as a key.
wallet_interface_delivery_form.evidence: A challenge is input to a PUF device comprising a physically unclonable function, PUF

ledger_access_permission.definition: Blockchain network built on an enterprise permissioned framework where participants and endorsement roles are configured by the operator for throughput and latency tuning.
ledger_access_permission.evidence: In a hyper ledger-based blockchain network system

ledger_access_permission.definition: Ledger where transaction execution and payload access are restricted to nodes whose characteristics satisfy data-associated policies, while other nodes see only identifiers.
ledger_access_permission.evidence: the transaction is executed at the DL node, and the transaction is inserted as a private transaction

ledger_access_permission.definition: Access to the distributed ledger is granted or restricted according to the geographic location of the requesting device or participant.
ledger_access_permission.evidence: the permission to access the distributed ledger being location based

consensus_finality.definition: Ledger state corrected by re-executing later operations and appending a new block rather than altering existing blocks.
consensus_finality.evidence: without changing any existing blocks of the blockchain, updating the ledger by adding to the current end

asset_reference_type.definition: Token price determined by a bonding curve function of circulating supply and supported by a deposited reserve pool rather than a pegged reference asset.
asset_reference_type.evidence: The bonding curve is changed as soon as the currency reserve reaches a certain minimum amount

asset_reference_type.definition: Crypto-asset rate determined by an algorithmic bonding curve over supply or history, rather than a reference asset peg or collateral.
asset_reference_type.evidence: a method for controlling a cryptocurrency based on a bonding curve predefined for a rate

asset_reference_type.definition: Token whose value references environmental attributes such as carbon dioxide offtake or emissions credits, not a physical commodity or currency.
asset_reference_type.evidence: manage transactions relating to assets, such as carbon dioxide ("CO2") offtake agreements

asset_reference_type.definition: Token issued in exchange for users' personal data and ad engagement, redeemable into currency or other crypto-assets via the platform.
asset_reference_type.evidence: Paying members for their data in blockchain crypto-tokens by providing Crypto-tokens to members

tokenisation_form.definition: Token representing ownership of extraterrestrial real property such as stars or star groupings, rather than a terrestrial or traditional asset.
tokenisation_form.evidence: off-world real property preferably comprises heavenly stars or groupings of heavenly stars

tokenisation_form.definition: Cryptocurrency whose value basis is an aggregate valuation of user-contributed raw data sets rather than a traditional asset.
tokenisation_form.evidence: valuing and regulating a data asset backed cryptocurrency

crypto_asset_function.definition: Token whose consumption or expenditure unlocks computer-implemented features, functionalities or licensed access to a digital product.
crypto_asset_function.evidence: associating computer-implemented features, functionalities, and/or digital asset rights with the consumption of consumable items

crypto_asset_function.definition: NFTs whose relational or causal data links them within a set, with fusion or burning creating new tokens from owned subsets.
crypto_asset_function.evidence: relational or causal data between different NFTs in a set of NFTs

minting_mechanism.definition: Tokens held in reserve and released to the market only when predefined performance metrics of the issuer or project are met.
minting_mechanism.evidence: The cryptocurrency company will issue the remaining 60 million tokens only per some formula, based on performance metrics being met.

minting_mechanism.definition: Units minted as rewards for verified real-world physical actions or activities rather than block validation or collateral locking.
minting_mechanism.evidence: allows for mining/minting of digital currency based on transactions and/or physical actions performed in the real world

minting_mechanism.definition: New units minted as a reward for verified physical electrical power output reported by the minting device.
minting_mechanism.evidence: The number of new value tokens they are entitled to create is determined by the amount of solar electric power they produce

finality_mechanism.definition: Finality decided by proposals whose measures count blocks mined by each network node, with re-proposal until a criterion is met.
finality_mechanism.evidence: based on the number of blocks within the blockchain that were mined by a respective node within the network of nodes

key_splitting_scheme.definition: Key shares are contributed via commitment and reveal or rescind transactions on a commitment channel formed between a node and a principal node.
key_splitting_scheme.evidence: submitted to a repository system by broadcasting a commitment transaction and a subsequent reveal or rescind transaction

network_topology.definition: Blockchain node communication built on named-data, information-centric networking with cached data packets at intermediate nodes.
network_topology.evidence: a blockchain based on information-centric networking (ICN)

network_topology.definition: Network topology where client nodes submit transactions in fixed time slots with a bounded delay for propagation to blockchain nodes.
network_topology.evidence: there is an upper-bound on the number of slots on the reception of the said transaction at an arbitrary blockchain node

ledger_mutability_model.definition: Ledger whose history can be at least partially edited or rewritten, e.g. via chameleon hash functions, rather than being strictly append-only.
ledger_mutability_model.evidence: the use of chameleon hash functions, so as to manipulate at least partially redactable blockchains

key_custody_control_model.definition: Redemption transaction requires cryptographic signatures from both the holder and a counterparty before it is valid and stored.
key_custody_control_model.evidence: receive a redeem transaction cryptographically signed by a private key of the party other than the first user

key_management_control_model.proposal: quantum random number generator key generation
key_management_control_model.definition: Private keys generated from quantum random number sources housed in tamper-resistant device casings.
key_management_control_model.evidence: The quantum random number generator may generate quantum-resilient random numbers to be used as private keys.

ledger_node_role.definition: Blockchain node built from dedicated hardware components such as smart network cards and smart contract chips offloading consensus and contract execution.
ledger_node_role.evidence: the blockchain node device includes the smart network card, at least one central processing unit, and a smart contract processing chip
